previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of chronic bilateral rotator cuff tears, septic arthritis of the left shoulder, aortic stenosis, and SIADH was admitted for worsening right shoulder pain radiating down the arm, swelling, and limited mobility. He had been managing pain with Tylenol and Tramadol, but symptoms had become intolerable. Imaging showed severe degenerative joint disease and rotator cuff tear, unchanged from prior studies. Arthrocentesis was performed, and joint fluid analysis revealed no infection, with no organisms seen on gram stain and no growth in culture. Inflammatory markers were only mildly elevated. Pain was managed with oxycodone initially, then transitioned with the addition of short-course ibuprofen. Hyponatremia remained stable on a normal diet with added salt. The patient improved clinically, with reduced pain and swelling, and was discharged home on a plan to continue pain medications, complete a three-day course of ibuprofen, and follow up with primary care and orthopedics.
